decisions.reason: After several years with only light visibility, this narrow mechanical niche has likely revealed limited standalone potential and its higher support complexity makes closing the option the more efficient use of resources.

This control technology sits in the firm's core automation domain, complements integrated water-engineering projects, and remains a relatively low-cost option to retain while value is realized across installations.

As a recent software-and-automation product closely aligned with the firm's move toward connected and data-driven infrastructure management, it is worth keeping because uncertainty can still resolve at modest continuation cost.
